subject: mathematics

core_competencies.justification: The whole chapter is the successive construction of the real number system: it starts with the counting numbers built from one-to-one correspondence, adds zero through Brahmagupta's rules, extends to the integers through debts and fortunes, defines the rational numbers as p/q with their equality, arithmetic and closure laws, shows the rationals are dense yet still leave gaps, introduces the irrationals through the diagonal of a unit square and pi, and finally unites the two into the unbroken real line. Along the way it develops the properties and representations of each set — placing rationals and irrationals on the number line, the absolute value as distance from zero, and the terminating-or-repeating decimal expansion as the test that separates rational from irrational.

adjunct_competencies.justification: The chapter narrates the evolution of numbers through the mathematicians and cultures who built it — the Lebombo and Ishango tally bones, the standardised weights of Lothal and Harappa, the Vedic names for powers of ten, Brahmagupta's definition of zero and his laws for debts and fortunes in the Brahmasphutasiddhanta, the bindu of the Bakhshali Manuscript, Baudhayana's Shulbasutra, Hippasus's proof, Aryabhata's approximation to pi, Madhava's infinite series and Lambert's proof — and closes with an explicit summary of that historical progression, so recognising these contributions is a genuine strand of the chapter rather than decoration.

Proof by contradiction is taught as a named technique and worked in full over eight steps to establish that the square root of 2 is irrational, and the student is then asked to reproduce it for the square roots of 3 and 5; alongside this, the chapter carries out a ruler-and-compass construction that produces a segment of length root 2 from a unit length and a perpendicular, extends it to root 3 and root 5, generalises it to root n, and closes with the square root spiral, so both proving from stated assumptions and constructing under given constraints are exercised directly.

dissolution_test: This chapter builds the student's ability to understand the real number system and the relationships between the number sets inside it by tracing the successive extension from natural numbers to integers, rationals, irrationals and finally the reals, representing each on the number line, and using the terminating-or-repeating character of the decimal expansion as the test that tells a rational number from an irrational one.
